claims.text: OrdersController.Create reads the caller id from the token's sub claim, maps request.Items to OrderItem objects, calls orderService.PlaceOrderAsync(customerId, items), and returns CreatedAtAction(nameof(Get), new { id = order.Id }, ToDto(order)).
CreatedAtAction produces a 201 Created response with a Location header built from the named action and route values, and the given value as the body.

OrdersController.Create contains no item-count check and no SaveChangesAsync call; OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync throws ArgumentException when items is empty, and ExceptionHandlingMiddleware maps ArgumentException to a 400 problem response.
ToDto builds an OrderDto from the order's Id, CustomerId, Status, PlacedAt and items mapped to OrderItemDto.
ProductsController takes DonHangDbContext and queries db.Products directly.
DonHang.Tests calls OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync directly, with fake dependencies and no HTTP request.
A controller should only read the request, call the layer below with plain values, and shape the result into a DTO and status code; business rules and database access belong in lower layers.
A rule placed in the controller is skipped by callers that do not come through HTTP, such as tests calling the business layer directly.

self_check.notes: Outline retargeted to stage-1 (DECISIONS.md §3, 2026-09-25): Create already delegates to OrderService. ProductsController's direct DbContext use is named as a shortcut and left for the tracing lesson. No action filters or model binding detail, per depth_notes.
